newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European '95 insurance business up 6.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: European '95 insurance business up 6.8 pct.

text.p: Insurance activities in Europe rose 6.8 percent in 1995, with premium volume more than 490 billion Ecus ($578 billion), the European Insurance Committee said on Thursday.
Life insurance business grew 7.5 percent and non-life insurance six percent, the committee said in a report covering 24 European countries.

Growth was lower than the previous year, however, "with companies principally having tried to consolidate their positions in the face of a very lively competitive situation exacerbated by the final phase of the completion of the Single Insurance Market", it said.
Insurance represented seven percent of Europe's Gross Domestic Product in 1995, compared with six percent in 1994, it said.
The survey found that Britain, France and Germany accounted for 70 percent of Europe's premium income and that there were significant differences between national markets.

Luxembourg has seen "astounding" growth, with increased turnover of more than 120 percent in 1995 and 673 percent since 1990 -- the result of opportunities offered by the new European single license system.
"Apart from Luxembourg, it is the markets of central and eastern Europe which are showing the strongest growth, with the exception of Hungary," the report said.

"Finland and Portugal have also undergone sharp growth in their premium income, mainly due to the growth in life insurance. On the other hand Spain, Norway, Sweden, Iceland and Ireland have recorded a fall in activity in 1995."

The number of insurance companies operating in Europe rose to 5,320 in 1995, up from 5,302 in 1994 -- but realignments and mergers and acquisitions have cut the number of local operators in countries including Spain, Belgium, Greece and France.
The number of operators in central and eastern Europe, however, has risen sharply since 1992. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
